member.name: T:TreeGrid.Wpf.Export.ExcelExporter
member.summary:
Writes an .xlsx workbook.
With the tree becomes Excel's own row grouping, so the collapse controls in the sheet margin mirror the grid's expanders. That is the only style that keeps the hierarchy genuinely interactive after export.

member.summary: Freeze the header row in the produced sheet.

member.name: P:TreeGrid.Wpf.Export.ExcelExporter.AddAutoFilter
member.summary: Add Excel's filter dropdowns to the header row.

member.summary: Writes the typed value where possible so Excel can sort and total the column, falling back to the formatted string only for values it cannot represent natively.

member.name: T:TreeGrid.Wpf.Export.PdfExporter
member.summary:
Renders the grid to PDF.
Column widths come from the grid's own resolved widths, scaled to the page. Using the on-screen proportions keeps the exported document recognisable as the thing the user was looking at.

member.name: P:TreeGrid.Wpf.Export.PdfExporter.IndentPerLevel
member.summary: Points of left padding applied per hierarchy level.

member.name: M:TreeGrid.Wpf.Export.PdfExporter.ResolveWidths(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{TreeGrid.Wpf.Columns.TreeGridColumn})
member.summary: Converts on-screen pixel widths into relative units. Columns that were never measured fall back to an equal share rather than collapsing to nothing.
